title: South Korea's NIS proposes widening intelligence collection on state-backed hacking groups
summary: ZDNet Korea reports that South Korea's National Intelligence Service put a partial amendment to its Cybersecurity Affairs Regulation up for public notice. It would widen cybersecurity intelligence collection to activity suspected of coming from international or state-backed hacking groups, and bar collecting data from state agencies unrelated to cyber threats. It would also require reports to the National Assembly's Intelligence Committee.
plain: South Korea's intelligence service has proposed a rule change letting it collect more information on suspected state-backed hackers, with reporting to parliament.
exec: A proposed rule would widen how South Korea's intelligence service gathers information on suspected state-backed hacking, per ZDNet Korea.
